title: Entanglement Requires Fluctuations at Conformal Interfaces
authors: Yuya Kusuki, Kosei Suzuyama, Yin Tang
abstract: We conjecture that the universal logarithmic coefficient for capacity of entanglement $c_{\mathrm{cap}}$ is bounded below by the corresponding entropy coefficient $c_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at conformal interfaces. We prove the bound in free boson and fermion CFTs and in holographic models with interface branes, and establish it using defect perturbation theory. Numerical calculations at interacting interfaces between the tricritical Ising and Ising CFTs further support the bound. Despite this constraint, capacity provides independent interface data. We construct interfaces with identical entropy and energy transmission coefficients but different capacity coefficients, and show that capacity can even increase as entropy decreases.
summary: This work establishes a theoretical bound relating the universal logarithmic coefficient of entanglement capacity ($c_{cap}$) to that of entanglement entropy ($c_{eff}$) at conformal interfaces. By proving this bound in several physical contexts, including free CFTs and holographic models, the authors demonstrate that capacity provides a distinct, measurable diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum correlations across boundaries.
main_problem: The paper investigates the relationship between entanglement entropy ($S_A$) and the capacity of entanglement ($C_A$) at quantum interfaces, specifically testing the conjecture that $c_{eff} \le c_{cap}$.
main_result: The conjectured bound $c_{eff} \le c_{cap}$ is proven in free CFTs and holographic models, and numerical calculations confirm that capacity provides independent data distinct from entropy.
method: The authors employ theoretical proofs using defect perturbation theory, replica trick calculations, and analyzing scaling laws derived from DMRG simulations on lattice models.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) connected by various interfaces, including free boson/fermion CFTs, holographic interface branes, and interacting systems like the tricritical Ising/Ising interface.
key_observables: Entanglement Entropy ($S_A$) and Capacity of Entanglement ($C_A$), characterized by their universal logarithmic coefficients ($c_{eff}$ and $c_{cap}$).
important_parameters: The interface coupling strengths, the size of the system ($L$), and the central charges of the constituent CFTs.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the applicability of CFT techniques, the use of replica geometry, and the validity of the holographic correspondence in certain limits.
figures_summary: Figures compare lattice coefficients ($c_{eff}/c$ and $c_{cap}/c$) against exact free-fermion curves, and show how capacity slopes can overtake entropy slopes at interfaces.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the conjecture in free field theories and holography, to providing rigorous proofs using defect perturbation theory, and finally validating the results through extensive numerical calculations on complex interacting lattice models.
why_interesting: The connection between entanglement measures like entropy and capacity is fundamental to understanding quantum correlations across boundaries, which has implications for quantum information flow and boundary physics in condensed matter systems.
